assumptions_and_boundaries.name: flatten_array_vec;array_value_view
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Generated flattening contract vocabulary is instantiated in the harness as target-local spec declarations; the public target body does not assume its postcondition.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: Vec::into_raw_parts_with_alloc
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Rust 1.96 decomposes the source Vec into pointer, length, capacity, and allocator before rebuilding a Vec<T, A>. The harness keeps this call and records only the raw-storage view relation needed to connect the returned pointer to flatten_array_vec.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: T::IS_ZST, checked_mul().expect, and unchecked_mul
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Rust 1.96 uses the ZST layout intrinsic to select checked length multiplication with the documented panic edge, and non-ZST unchecked length/capacity multiplication justified by the existing allocation address-space invariant. The harness keeps the branch and arithmetic shape while trusting these source-backed intrinsic/panic facts.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: ptr.cast() from *mut [T; N] to *mut T
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The source pointer cast is modeled as the layout-identical array-to-element raw-pointer conversion needed before Vec::<T, A>::from_raw_parts_in. Verus does not support raw pointer .cast() directly in verified code, so the harness isolates only that cast in a named external boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: Vec::<T, A>::from_raw_parts_in
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The final unsafe reconstruction remains the allocator/raw-pointer/provenance boundary: Rust requires the raw parts to describe the same allocation, capacity, alignment, and initialized prefix. The harness preserves the call and carries the flattened initialized view through to Vec@.

notes: The public target method is executable and non-external-body: it keeps the Rust 1.96 flow `let (ptr, len, cap, alloc) = self.into_raw_parts_with_alloc();` then the ZST checked-multiply panic path or non-ZST unchecked length/capacity multiply path, then `Vec::<T, A>::from_raw_parts_in(ptr.cast(), new_len, new_cap, alloc)`. This is a B proof modulo named source-backed allocator, intrinsic, panic, raw-pointer/provenance, and unsafe reconstruction boundaries, not an assume_specification or a public-target external_body.
